papers.title: Second order Recurrences, quadratic number fields and cyclic codes
papers.abstract: Wall-Sun-Sun primes (shortly WSS primes) are defined as those primes $p$ such that the period of the Fibonacci recurrence is the same modulo $p$ and modulo $p^2.$ This concept has been generalized recently to certain second order recurrences whose characteristic polynomials admit as a zero the principal unit of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d}),$ for some integer $d>0.$ Primes of the latter type we call $WSS(d).$ They correspond to the case when $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ is not $p$-rational. For such a prime $p$ we study the weight distributions of the cyclic codes over $\mathbb{F}_p$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$ whose check polynomial is the reciprocal of the said characteristic polynomial. Some of these codes are MDS (reducible case) or NMDS (irreducible case).

papers.title: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugates
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be chosen uniformly from the geometric isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and $\delta_E$ be the minimum degree of isogenies from $E$ to its Frobenius conjugate $E^{(p)}$. We establish bounds for the smoothness probability of $\delta_E$ and hence affirm Wesolowski's $p^{1/3+o(1)}$ attack on the supersingular endomorphism ring problem is unconditional. We also establish a uniform asymptotic formula, with a main term expressed in terms of Dirichlet $L$ values, for the probability that a connection isogeny of degree $n$ exists between $E$ and $E^{(p)}$.

papers.title: Three Quadratic Recurrences Modulo 3: What We Can Prove and What We Can Guess
papers.abstract: We study three innocent-looking recurrences modulo $3$, each built from squares of two earlier terms. One of them turns out to be secretly $\textit{linear}$, and we can compute its periods exactly. One is a $\textit{permutation}$ hiding a small, perfectly orderly piece inside a large, random-looking one. The third looks thoroughly random, but it still has a few provable features. Along the way we meet open problems that need nothing beyond a first course in abstract algebra to state. This paper is a starting point, not the final word in any sense.

papers.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $\eta_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{\eta_i,\eta_j\in S:\eta_i\neq\eta_j}|\mathcal N(\eta_i-\eta_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.

papers.title: MDS codes containing a fixed subcode over finite field extensions
papers.abstract: Let $2\le k\le n$ and let $U\le\mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a fixed $(k-1)$-dimensional linear code. We study the $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) codes over finite extensions of $\mathbb{F}_q$ that contain the scalar extension of $U$. Our approach constructs an auxiliary linear code from \(U\). Its full-weight words characterize the desired MDS completions. We prove that \(U\) admits an \([n,k]\) MDS completion over some finite extension of \(\mathbb{F}_q\) if and only if \(d(U)\ge n-k+1\). When this condition holds, the number of these MDS codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$ is \[\#\left\{W\le\mathbb{F}_{q^m}^n:U\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^m}\subseteq W,\ \dim_{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}} W=k,\ W\text{ is MDS}\right\}=\frac{\chi_{\delta_GM(G)}(q^m)}{q^m-1},\] where $G$ is a generator matrix of $U$, $\delta_GM(G)$ is its represented derived matroid, and $\chi_{\delta_GM(G)}$ is its characteristic polynomial. In particular, the formula determines existence over each extension field and the least extension degree for which such an MDS code exists. Examples show that these counts may distinguish different representations of the same column matroid, while monomially inequivalent codes may have identical counts over every finite extension.

papers.title: Proofs of strong forms of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture and a complex analogue
papers.abstract: We prove two universality theorems for neural networks consisting of a single neuron. First we prove a strong form of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture on neurons over finite fields, where the activation function is a certain modification of the discrete logarithm, using the Weil bound on multiplicative character sums over finite fields. Then we show a generalisation of Aizenberg's universality theorem for complex binary neurons with a weight vector independent of the target function, positively answering another question in the literature. The proof of the latter uses an equidistribution theorem for the dilates of certain maps into tori.

papers.title: Brauer--Manin obstruction for Weil restrictions
papers.abstract: For a quasi-projective variety $X$ defined over a number field $k$, let $X'$ be its Weil restriction with respect to a finite field extension $k/k'$. We prove that the Brauer--Manin set of $X$ agrees with the Brauer--Manin set of $X'$. We also prove the agreement for Brauer--Manin set of them given by $\mathrm{Br}_1$.

papers.title: Fine points of the moduli space of cubic rational maps
papers.abstract: A rational point of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_3$ of cubic rational maps is fine if its conjugacy class contains a map defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and coarse otherwise. In the invariants $\xi_0,\dots,\xi_5$ that embed $\mathcal{M}_3$ in $\mathbb{P}(2,2,3,3,4,6)$, we prove that a point with trivial automorphism group is fine if and only if the quaternion algebra $(-m_{12},-2\xi_0)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ splits, where $m_{12}=\frac{1}{3}\xi_0^2\xi_1+\xi_0\xi_4-\xi_3^2$; we give the analogous criterion on the locus $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution and show that all other strata are fine. The proof is constructive and yields an explicit descent. We prove that the obstruction class is unramified along every divisor of the compactification, that a prime $p\ge 5$ obstructs only if the point reduces modulo $p$ into the closure of one of the two codimension-two loci $\mathcal{L}_1$, $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution, and that $\mathcal{M}_3$ has transverse $A_1$-singularities along both, above which the class ramifies; local densities predict that $\mathcal{L}_2$ is met modulo $p$ with probability $\asymp 1/p$, so that it carries the obstruction. A census of all 214,260,288 rational points of weighted moduli height at most 7 agrees with this mechanism and supports the conjecture that the proportion of fine points tends to zero like $(\log B)^{-1/2}$.

papers.title: On the Torsion Subgroup of the N\'eron--Severi Group
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit bound for the torsion subgroup of the N\'eron--Severi group of a smooth projective complex variety. The proof combines the Diophantine-approximation method of Ziyang Gao and the author (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22285) with Lefschetz fibrations. As an application, we deduce an explicit bound for the torsion sections of a traceless abelian scheme over a complex curve.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the maximal function field with the third largest genus in characteristic $3$
papers.abstract: Let $n$ be a positive integer and define $q=3^n$. It is well known that there exists a maximal function field $Z_3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3=q(q-1)/6$ and that $g_3$ is the third largest genus a maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ can have. In this article we show that any maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3$ is isomorphic to $Z_3$. This extends previously known uniqueness result for the largest and second largest genera of maximal curves.

papers.title: Characterising canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We study Brantner-Taelman's canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties and characterise their (quasi)canonical lifts in terms of rational $p$-adic Hodge theoretic data. We also show that these canonical lifts need not be of CM type and that the associated local Galois representations need not split as sums of twists of unramified representations, in contrast to classical results for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces.

papers.title: Height growth of rational self-maps
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field or a function field of a curve. Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over $K$, and let $h_H\geq1$ be an ample Weil height. Let $\lambda_1(f)$ denote the first dynamical degree of $f$. We show that there is a constant $C_{f,h_H}>0$ such that, for any $n\geq1$ and any point $P\in X(\overline{K})$ with well-defined forward orbit, $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2(d-1)}\lambda_1(f)^n$ if $\lambda_1(f)>1$, and $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2d}$ if $\lambda_1(f)=1$. Over number fields, the proof combines a new uniform upper bound for arithmetic degrees with a uniform comparison of point heights. Over function fields, it relies on the corresponding uniform upper bound for geometric degrees on a projective model.

papers.title: Cross numbers and the characterization of finite abelian groups by length sets
papers.abstract: The Characterization Problem asks whether a finite abelian group with Davenport constant at least four is determined, up to isomorphism, by its system of length sets. This is a central inverse problem in non-unique factorization theory: it asks whether the possible numbers of irreducible factors retain enough information to recover the underlying class group. For rings of integers of algebraic number fields, an affirmative answer means that the ideal class group can be recovered from these factorization lengths alone. We resolve this problem for all homocyclic groups $C_n^r$: if $G$ is a finite abelian group with $\mathsf D(G)\ge4$ and $\mathcal L(G)=\mathcal L(C_n^r)$, then $G\cong C_n^r$. The cross number of a sequence is the sum of the reciprocals of the orders of its terms. This weighted measure of sequence length links zero-sum theory with half-factoriality, and determining its maximal value for minimal zero-sum sequences is a longstanding extremal problem. We also obtain an exact formula for the maximal cross number of minimal zero-sum sequences over subsets whose minimum distance is divisible by the rank of the ambient group minus one. For $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$ with $1<n_1\mid\cdots\mid n_r$ and $r\ge\max\{2,n_r-2\}$, we prove \[ \mathsf K(G,r-1)=1+(r-1)\sum_{p\mid n_1} \left(1-p^{-\mathsf v_p(n_1)}\right), \] which is a key ingredient in resolving the Characterization Problem for homocyclic groups.

papers.title: Hartl's dictionary and a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with complex multiplication
papers.abstract: We update Hartl's dictionary between $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog to include aspects related to the Hodge--Tate filtration in $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog, the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration. Using this update, we establish a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with abelian Tannakian structure group, matching a result of Howe--Klevdal in the $p$-adic setting. A special case of this result says that a formal Drinfeld module over an equicharacteristic local field has complex multiplication if and only if the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration on its $z$-adic Tate module is algebraic.

papers.title: Dynamical Chowla conjecture for polynomials of several variables
papers.abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the mean value of the Liouville function at non-square one-variable polynomials is zero. This conjecture is a generalization of the prime number theorem (PNT). In 2022, Bergelson and Richter established a dynamical generalization of this form of the PNT. For non-square multivariate polynomials, one also expects that Chowla's conjecture is true. In this article, we extend Bergelson and Richter's result to multivariate polynomials whose Birch rank is sufficiently large in terms of their degree. We also establish analogous results for averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.

papers.title: Analogues of Traverso's Isogeny Conjecture for Some Unitary p-Divisible Groups
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $\Bbbk$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Two invariants worthy of study for a $p$-divisible group $X$ over $\Bbbk$ are its isogeny cutoff $b_X$, which measures the amount of $p$-torsion necessary to determine the Newton polygon of $X$, and its minimal height $q_X$, which measures its distance to the closest minimal $p$-divisible group (in the sense of Oort). Traverso's Isogeny Conjecture predicts a bound on $b_X$ in terms of its height and dimension. The conjecture was proved in [NV07] and a refinement was given in [LNV13]; the latter also gives a bound on $q_X$. In this paper, we study these invariants when restricting to the class of supersingular unitary $p$-divisible groups $X$ of signature $(a,g-a)$, where $0 < a < g$, for $p > 2$, and prove further refinements on their bounds purely in terms of $a$. In particular, we provide a complete description of the possible values of $q_X$. Finally, we rephrase our results in the language of the $\mathrm{BT}_m$ stratifications of characteristic-$p$ fibers of Shimura varieties for $\mathrm{GU}(a, g-a)$ in the case of an inert prime $p > 2$.

papers.title: Explicit Kodaira-Spencer maps over PEL Shimura varieties
papers.abstract: The goal of our work is to construct a class of morphisms between two canonical line bundles on integral models of PEL Shimura varieties via Kodaira--Spencer maps, and explicitly compute such morphisms and their effects on the canonical metrics of line bundles. This result provides a concrete method for comparing two canonical line bundles and the corresponding arithmetic intersection numbers. In particular, it allows us to give an explicit relationship between the height functions defined by these two line bundles.

papers.title: Some arithmetical aspects of the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that any counter-example to the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture with integral coefficients and determinant of its Jacobian matrix equals one, has only paths of asymptotic values that can contain only finitely many points of the planar integral lattice. The second part of our paper gives some nontrivial applications of the theory of certain Theta functions to the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture over the real field, and over the complex field.

papers.title: Intersecting a curve in an abelian variety with multiples of another curve
papers.abstract: Levin asked what can be said about the locus of points lying on a given curve in $\mathbb{G}_m^n$ that have a non-zero integer power on another given curve in $\mathbb{G}_m^n$ for $n \geq 3$. We give a definite answer to the abelian analog of Levin's question, proving what is predicted by the Zilber-Pink conjecture in this case. An important ingredient in our proof is a strengthening of a height inequality by Vojta and R\'emond.

papers.title: Inequalities and asymptotics for hook numbers in two partition functions of MacMahon and Andrews
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent studies of hook length biases in restricted partitions, we investigate the total number of hooks of fixed length in two partition functions introduced by MacMahon and Andrews. In $1916$, MacMahon proved that the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part appears with multiplicity one equals the number of partitions of $n$ into parts that are even or congruent to $3 \pmod{6}$. For a positive integer $r$, let $A_r(n)$ count the partitions of $n$ in which every part occurring an odd number of times occurs at least $2r+1$ times, and let $B_r(n)$ count the partitions into parts that are even or congruent to $2r+1 \pmod{4r+2}$. Andrews proved that $A_r(n)=B_r(n)$ for all positive integers $r$ and nonnegative integers $n$, thereby recovering MacMahon's identity as the special case $r=1$. We derive generating functions and asymptotic formulas for the total numbers of hooks of lengths $1$, $2$, and $3$ in both partition classes, employing Wright's circle method. These asymptotic formulas yield several hook length bias results. In particular, for sufficiently large $n$, the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $1$-hooks than the $A_r$-type partitions, whereas for hook lengths $2$ and $3$, the bias is reversed when $r=1$ and favors the $B_r$-type partitions when $r\geq 2$. We also establish asymptotic inequalities among hook numbers of different lengths within each partition class. Finally, for fixed hook lengths $\ell\in\{1,2,3\}$, we prove that the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $\ell$-hooks than the $B_{r+1}$-type partitions for sufficiently large $n$. These results reveal systematic asymptotic patterns in the distribution of small hook lengths across the two partition families.

papers.title: Colored Partitions and Minimal Excludants
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce the concept of minimal excludants in colored partitions and extend it to the framework of least $r$-gaps. In particular, we focus on $k$-colored partitions and cubic partitions, deriving the generating functions for the sums of minimal excludants and least $r$-gaps, and analyzing their asymptotic behaviors. Notably, the presented theory is comprehensively extended by the systematic generalization of each result for minimal excludants in $k$-colored partitions to the case of least $r$-gaps. We introduce generalized cubic partitions and discover the minimal excludant, as well as several additional results.

papers.title: Temporal central limit theorem for mixed-radix odometer discrepancy
papers.abstract: We consider the local discrepancy for the number of visits of the orbit of $0$ under a mixed-radix odometer to intervals near the origin. Both the length of the orbit and the endpoint of the visited interval are chosen independently and uniformly at random. Under a Feller-type condition and an explicit condition ensuring that the finite random-time clock can be approximated by a Haar clock on the fluctuation scale, we obtain a temporal central limit theorem for the discrepancy, with an explicit Kolmogorov-Smirnov rate of convergence. This extends and strengthens the fixed-base temporal central limit theorem of Levin and Merzbach to the mixed-radix setting.

papers.title: Pointwise ergodic theorems along oscillating sequences
papers.abstract: We establish the first pointwise convergence result for nonconventional ergodic averages modeled along a large class of oscillating sequences, treating, for example, orbits of the form $\big(\lfloor n^d\sin(e\pi n)\rfloor\big)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$. More specifically, for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ equipped with an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T\colon X\to X$ and every $f\in L^p_{\mu}(X)$ with $p\in(1,\infty]$, we prove that the limit \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^Nf\big(T^{\lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor}x\big)\quad\text{exists for $\mu$-a.e. $x\in X$,} \] where $P$ is a non-constant polynomial with real coefficients, $\psi$ is $1$-periodic and real-analytic, and $\alpha$ has irrationality exponent smaller than $1+\sqrt{\operatorname{deg}(P)+1}$. On the one hand, the latter assumption is satisfied by a.e. $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, and, on the other hand, our result covers any of the following concrete orbits \[ \lfloor n\cos(e\pi n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\lfloor n^{37}\sin(n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\big\lfloor \sqrt{2}n^{10}e^{\sin(\pi (\sqrt[5]{7}+1) n)}\big\rfloor\text{,}\quad \big\lfloor \big((\log 2) n^3+e n\big)e^{e^{\cos(\pi \sqrt{2} n)}}\big\rfloor\text{.} \] The proof employs the so-called one-frequency circle method for estimating exponential sums with phases $\big(\xi \lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor\big)_{1\le n\le N}$, but the major arc approximants of our exponential sums do not consist of their direct continuous counterparts. In the major arc regime we decouple the $\psi$-oscillatory part of the phase from the polynomial one, and approximate the exponential sum by $\int_0^1\big(\frac{1}{N}\int_0^Ne^{2\pi i\xi P(t)\psi( s)}dt\big)ds$. This represents a novel phenomenon for problems of this kind, and, interestingly, our proof exploits the coefficient-free variational estimates of Radon-type operators.

papers.title: Modular Existential Closedness
papers.abstract: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n, j(\tau_1), \ldots, j(\tau_n)) \in V$ with $\tau_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouch\'e's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.

papers.title: Properties C and D fail for $C_n^r$ whenever $n \equiv 2 \bmod 4, n\geq 6$ and $r\geq 4$
papers.abstract: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant (zero-sums of length exactly $n$) and $\eta(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant. Properties C and D of Gao et al.\ assert that every sequence of the extremal length without the relevant zero-sums has the form $T^{n-1}$. For even $n$ they imply $s(C_n^r)=2^r(n-1)+1$ and $\eta(C_n^r)=(2^r-1)(n-1)+1$. G.~Wang recently disproved both for $C_6^r$, $r\ge4$. We prove that both fail for $C_n^r$ for every $n\equiv2\pmod4$ with $n\ge6$ and every $r\ge4$. More precisely, for these $n$ we have: $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+2^{r-2}+1$.

papers.title: Finite-sum Identities and Supercongruences for Cubes of Catalan Numbers
papers.abstract: Let $C_k=\binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ be the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $p$ be an odd prime. We establish exact finite-sum identities that, together with known binomial supercongruences and reductions of Sun, yield $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{16^k}\equiv2-24y^2-\frac{5p^2}{2y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{(-8)^k}\equiv-1-48y^2-\frac{33p^2}{16y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+4y^2\equiv1\pmod4$. We also evaluate the corresponding sum with denominator $16^k(k+1)^2$, and obtain two weighted Catalan supercongruences. The finite identities follow from the ratios of consecutive summands, symmetry of double sums, and telescoping. All endpoint terms are retained over the rational numbers before any modular reduction. In each bilinear identity, one endpoint denominator equals $p$; its cancellation produces the necessary term of order $p^2$. The precise arithmetic inputs are stated separately.

papers.title: A symmetric extension of Zhao's series for $\zeta(5)$
papers.abstract: We prove a four-parameter extension of Zhao's series for $\zeta(5)$. Restricting a Wilf-Zeilberger seed of Au to a hyperplane, we obtain a summand in five parameters with zero sum that is symmetric under all their permutations. Summing it from two different starting points gives two trigonometric closed forms, which we prove by Guillera's periodicity argument. The proof is self-contained, and also gives a companion series for $1/\pi^2$, which we have not found in the literature. Specializing the parameters at roots of unity, we obtain Borwein-Bradley-type identities whose products depend only on $x^2$, $x^3$, $x^4$ or $x^5$. Their Taylor coefficients are Ap\'ery-like series for odd zeta values and for products of zeta values. In particular, we prove five identities conjectured by Au.

papers.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
papers.abstract: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $\Delta(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $\Delta(E)$ when $d$ is odd. If $M_{GP,d}(p)$ denotes the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression, then, for every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.

papers.title: Congruences modulo powers of $7$ for partitions with colored odd parts
papers.abstract: Let $a_k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ in which even parts occur in one color and odd parts may occur in $k$ colors. We prove infinite families of congruences modulo powers of $7$ for $a_k(n)$ when $k \in \{4,5,7\}$. For each positive integer $\alpha$, let $\lambda_{k,\alpha}$ be the least nonnegative solution of $24\lambda_{k,\alpha}\equiv-(k-2)\pmod{7^\alpha}$. Then, we show that \[ a_k(7^\alpha n+\lambda_{k,\alpha}) \equiv 0\pmod{7^{\lfloor(\alpha+1)/2\rfloor}} \] for every nonnegative integer $n$. These results extend congruences modulo $7$ of Hirschhorn and Sellers (2026) and complement Chen's (2025) congruences for the reciprocal crank parity function $a_3(n)$.

papers.title: On explicit formulas for Grassmannian polylogarithms and Gelfand-MacPherson forms
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Goncharov by showing that his Grassmannian $n$-logarithm can be recovered by integrating the Borel invariant form on the symmetric space $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(\mathbf{C})/\mathrm{SU}(n)$ over a naturally defined ideal simplex. As corollaries, we recover the finiteness of primitive canonical integrals of Brown and the evaluation for wheel graphs of Brown and Schnetz. We also compute explicitly the Gelfand-MacPherson forms for powers of the first Pontryagin class and give a general integral formula for the Gelfand-MacPherson forms associated to each component of the Pontryagin character.
